lines.trans: Respected chef, step right up and choose knives!
Look what a sharp and thin blade!
Careful, this blade is sharp as a dagger.
But here the metal is too soft.
This is the best strong steel for the kitchen!
Don't deceive me, I am an experienced chef.
One cannot cut meat with such a knife.
Then look at this Japanese knife.
Craftsmen made it from hard steel.
Yes, this knife rests in the hand perfectly.
How much does such an excellent tool cost?
For you I will give it for only three thousand.
Fine, I am taking this knife.
In my kitchen sharp order is needed!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'only'.
Secondary conversational sense ('in all, in total') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: They will give only eight years.

examples.text: Предлагаю чистосердечное признание. Дадут всего восемь лет.
examples.trans: I suggest a full confession. They'll give you only eight years.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: выбирать слова = to choose one's words

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'ideally'.

examples.trans: The kitchen must be ideally clean!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'tool; instrument' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('musical instrument') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Так, мы не шутим, понял? Давай инструмент страшнее.
examples.trans: Right, we are not joking, understood? Find a scarier tool.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dagger' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The blade is sharp as a dagger.

examples.text: Осторожно, этот клинок острый, как кинжал.
examples.trans: Careful, this blade is sharp as a dagger.

meanings.en: blade of a knife or sword
meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'blade, sword-blade' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Careful, this blade is very sharp.

examples.text: Осторожно, этот клинок острый, как кинжал.
examples.trans: Careful, this blade is sharp as a dagger.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lie', forming an aspectual pair with 'полежать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'blade, cutting edge' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У этого ножа очень острое лезвие.
examples.trans: This knife has a very sharp blade.

examples.text: Посмотрите, какое острое и тонкое лезвие!
examples.trans: Look what a sharp and thin blade!

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'metal', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('heavy metal music') (тяжёлый металл) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я вообще в школе тяжёлый металл любила!
examples.trans: In school I actually loved heavy metal!
The door is made of metal.
But here the metal is too soft.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'soft', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('tender') (tender and pleasant to chew) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мясо должно стать мягким и сочным.
examples.trans: The meat must become tender and juicy.

examples.text: У тебя очень милые мягкие кудри.
examples.trans: You have very sweet, soft curls.
But here the metal is too soft.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'meat', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'it is not allowed'.
Secondary conversational sense ('impossible, can't') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to lie to') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Потому что она простая. Её все обманывают.
examples.trans: Because she's naive. Everybody cheats her.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('experienced').

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'carefully'.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sharp; spicy').
Secondary conversational sense ('spicy, hot (food)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There's fishing line and a sharp hook here.

examples.text: Здесь леска и острый крючок. Это очень больно!
examples.trans: There's fishing line and a sharp hook here. It's very painful!

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'отдавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to give back') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He will hand over the money.

examples.text: Потом надо отдать москвичам твои деньги из подвала.
examples.trans: Then I have to give your money from the basement to the Moscow people.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') (это мне подходит = that suits me) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a look', forming an aspectual pair with 'смотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch (a film) through') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'чный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('durable, sturdy, strong').

examples.trans: This is the best strong steel.

examples.text: Это лучшая прочная сталь для кухни!
examples.trans: This is the best strong steel for the kitchen!

meanings.en: to cut, to slice, to carve
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cut, to slice', paired with 'разрезать'.

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'hand'.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.
Secondary conversational sense ('what a lot of!') (in exclamations) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'таль'). Common feminine noun meaning 'steel' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The knife is made of hard steel.

examples.text: Это лучшая прочная сталь для кухни!
examples.trans: This is the best strong steel for the kitchen!

examples.text: Его сделали мастера из твёрдой стали.
examples.trans: Craftsmen made it from hard steel.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cost'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to be worth') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And how much does the console cost?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hard, firm').

examples.text: Мастера сделали клинок из твёрдой стали.
examples.trans: Craftsmen made the blade from hard steel.

examples.text: Его сделали мастера из твёрдой стали.
examples.trans: Craftsmen made it from hard steel.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'subtle', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: That was a very subtle move.

examples.text: У нее тонкий вкус в искусстве.
examples.trans: She has delicate taste in art.
That was a very subtle move!

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('three') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.trans: We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: adjective/participle used in formal address

examples.text: Уважаемый ветеран, перед вами внук предателя!
examples.trans: Esteemed veteran, before you is the grandson of a traitor!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Japanese').

examples.trans: Wow, a tape recorder! A Japanese one!
